/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 06 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2991 (159)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5074 (371)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2135 (81)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1514 (6)
Baltic Handysize Index: 824 (3)
CAPESIZE
The positive momentum seen yesterday extended firmly into today, with both basins maintaining strong upward traction and showing little sign of easing. Market sentiment remains buoyant, underpinned by consistent activity and improving rate levels across the board. The BCI 182 5TC index rose by $3,368 to $46,017, reflecting the strengthening fundamentals. C5 gained $0.960 to $15.710, while C3 advanced by $1.184 to $36.909. In the Pacific, the tone remained resolutely positive, with healthy volumes and another busy trading day. The presence of three miners on C5, alongside a steady flow of tender cargoes, provided a solid foundation. Offers on C5 were initially heard in the low-to-mid $16s, with fixtures reportedly concluded at $15.50 before climbing through $15.90 and reaching $16.10 by the close. The Atlantic basin also gathered momentum, with sentiment improving on the back of increased activity. On C3, bids continued to firm, with reports of fixtures at $36.50 and $36.90, while offers pushed beyond $37. In the North Atlantic, volumes have picked up and a tightening tonnage list is adding further support to rates.
PANAMAX
In the Atlantic brokers report limited trading activity, however, with the fronthaul market strengthening sentiment has improved and available tonnage is said to be thinning. P2A is described by market participants as continuing its bullish run supported by increased mineral and grain fixing volumes prompting owners to raise offers in an effort to secure levels above recently concluded fixtures. In Asia, sentiment is mirroring the Atlantic, with positivity prevailing. Australian and North Pacific exports are reported as active, with fixture rates continuing their upward trajectory. Period activity was evident, with several fixtures noted, including Classic reportedly covering a North Coast South America trans Atlantic requirement on short period. The P5TC gained $726 to close at $19,216.

Atlantic
The scrubber fitted Patroklis (81,149 2017) Karaikal 29 April was reported fixed to Cofco for an East Coast South America fronthaul at $19,000. LV Star (79,252 2012) open Gibraltar 13/15 May fixed a North Coast South America fronthaul at $25,000 with the charterers undisclosed. The Captain V. Madias (79,501 2012) open Algeciras/Gibraltar for prompt dates was reported placed on subjects although further details have yet to emerge. The scrubber fitted J Mare (81,732 2020) open Gibraltar 17 May was reported fixed on subjects for a fronthaul trip, with some brokers suggesting it was for a trip via the US Gulf to Japan with Messrs Mitsubishi.

SUPRAMAX
A rather positional day for the sector, sentiment improved from the South Atlantic as brokers spoke of better levels of enquiry. However from the US Gulf brokers spoke of a mixed bag as fresh trans Atlantic business slowed somewhat. The Future (56,128 2012) open Barranquilla 10 May was heard to have been placed on subjects basis delivery New Orleans trip NC South America intention grains in the upper $19,000s. From Asia, little fresh information surfaced but some said better levels of fresh enquiry were seen. The 11TC average finished up $78 at $19,136.
HANDYSIZE
The market experienced another flat day overall, with the BHSI inching up by just 3 points to reach 824, and the 7TC average increasing slightly by $54, settling at $14,828. In both the Continent and Mediterranean regions, demand continues to be sluggish, leading many owners to consider ballasting or re-evaluating their rate expectations downward. The South Atlantic and US Gulf remained subdued due to lack of fresh demand, leaving rates largely flat. Over in Asia, activity is still muted as the market struggles to gather momentum, not helped by ongoing holidays in the region. Overall, the market continues to lack clear direction.

Market Fundamentals
China's Manufacturing PMI

China’s manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) eased 0.1 points from the prior month to 50.3 in April, recording the second consecutive month above the 50-mark indicating expansion, National Bureau of Statistics data show. Meanwhile, after reaching a high in April, the Chinese Steel Logistics Committee (CSLC) steel sector PMI fell 1.4 points to 49.2 in April, indicating contraction.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher again in response to much firmer physical market, as the index gains another $3,368. The biggest increase was in the May contract with 40300 paid, followed buy June with 36800 trading. The May v Jun spread widened and strengthened to a high of 3800. Pressure built during the afternoon session however, with 39000 and 35500 sold May and Jun respectively. The range on Q3 was 31400-32200 and Q4 31250-31600, with the Q3 v Q4 widening out to 600. Huge volume went through on the Cal27 between 26150-26350 and similarly the Cal28, with a range of 228750-23000.

PMX
PMX pushed higher than yesterday’s close, showing a strong index gain of +726. May traded at a low of 20150 and was bid up to 20800, however it lacked support and closed at 20250. June traded in a large range between 20000 and 21500. July held a narrow $300 range, trading up to 20700, which caused the June/July spread to reach 650. Q3 printed from a low of 19800 up to 20300 back to 19800 at close. Q4 traded between 17700 and 18250. On the back end, Cal27 traded around 15000, while Cal28 saw a few clips trade at 13900.

SMX + HANDY
The SMX market was well supported, shadowing the positive momentum seen in the Cape and Pmx markets. May traded 17750 - 18000, Jun 18400 - 18850, Jul 18150 - 18400 and Q3 to a high of 17900. Q4 traded between 15900 – 16200 and Q1 12250 – 12400. Cal27 v Cal28 was traded between 950 – 1000, Cal27 trading 13100 – 13225 and Cal28 12075 – 12250. Very limited liquidity in Handy market, in particular offer side, as just the Jun trading traded higher in a clip at 15900.

Carbon
EU carbon markets ticked �0.50/eua higher at the front of the curve today, with more modest gains observed in the deferred contracts. The strengthening market reflected new reports of a Middle East peace deal, leading to higher trading levels midday before retreating in the afternoon. Today's Commitment of Traders report, which includes data through last week, indicated a second consecutive decrease in the net long positions of Investment Funds to 35m EUAs. While this level remains high by most historical standards, it represents only a fraction of the levels seen late last year and early January.

Market Fundamentals
China's Manufacturing PMI
China’s manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI)
eased 0.1 points from the prior month to 50.3 in April,
recording the second consecutive month above the 50-mark
indicating expansion, National Bureau of Statistics data
show. Meanwhile, after reaching a high in April, the Chinese
Steel Logistics Committee (CSLC) steel sector PMI fell 1.4
points to 49.2 in April, indicating contraction.
Trading Commentary
Cape Routes
C5 had another strong day, gaining value throughout. The c5
may contract traded up to 15.25 a few times before closing
slightly lower at 15.20. June and July contracts also rose,
reaching 14.40 and 13.65 respectively. Meanwhile, the C3
market increased early, with June hitting 34.95, but later
pulled back and closed lower.
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher again in response to much
ﬁrmer physical market, as the index gains another $3,368.
The biggest increase was in the May contract with 40300
paid, followed buy June with 36800 trading. The May v Jun
spread widened and strengthened to a high of 3800.
Pressure built during the afternoon session however, with
39000 and 35500 sold May and Jun respectively. The range
on Q3 was 31400-32200 and Q4 31250-31600, with the Q3 v
Q4 widening out to 600. Huge volume went through on the
Cal27 between 26150-26350 and similarly the Cal28, with a
range of 228750-23000.
PMX
PMX pushed higher than yesterday’s close, showing a strong
index gain of +726. May traded at a low of 20150 and was bid
up to 20800, however it lacked support and closed at 20250.
June traded in a large range between 20000 and 21500. July
held a narrow $300 range, trading up to 20700, which caused
the June/July spread to reach 650. Q3 printed from a low of
19800 up to 20300 back to 19800 at close. Q4 traded
between 17700 and 18250. On the back end, Cal27 traded
around 15000, while Cal28 saw a few clips trade at 13900.
SMX + HANDY
The SMX market was well supported, shadowing the positive
momentum seen in the Cape and Pmx markets. May traded
17750 - 18000, Jun 18400 - 18850, Jul 18150 - 18400 and Q3
to a high of 17900. Q4 traded between 15900 – 16200 and
Q1 12250 – 12400. Cal27 v Cal28 was traded between 950 –
1000, Cal27 trading 13100 – 13225 and Cal28 12075 – 12250.
Very limited liquidity in Handy market, in particular oﬀer
side, as just the Jun trading traded higher in a clip at 15900.Cape 180 5TC

EU carbon markets ticked €0.50/eua higher at the front of
the curve today, with more modest gains observed in the
deferred contracts. The strengthening market reﬂected new
reports of a Middle East peace deal, leading to higher
trading levels midday before retreating in the afternoon.
Today's Commitment of Traders report, which includes data
through last week, indicated a second consecutive decrease
in the net long positions of Investment Funds to 35m EUAs.
While this level remains high by most historical standards, it
represents only a fraction of the levels seen late last year and
early January.

Meanwhile, after reaching a high in April, the Chinese Steel Logistics Committee (CSLC) steel sector PMI fell 1.4 points to 49.2 in April, indicating contraction. Trading Commentary Cape Routes C5 had another strong day, gaining value throughout. The c5 may contract traded up to 15.25 a few times before closing slightly lower at 15.20. June and July contracts also rose, reaching 14.40 and 13.65 respectively. Meanwhile, the C3 market increased early, with June hitting 34.95, but later pulled back and closed lower. Cape The Cape FFA curve rallied higher again in response to much firmer physical market, as the index gains another $3,368. The biggest increase was in the May contract with 40300 paid, followed buy June with 36800 trading. The May v Jun spread widened and strengthened to a high of 3800. Pressure built during the afternoon session however, with 39000 and 35500 sold May and Jun respectively. The range on Q3 was 31400-32200 and Q4 31250-31600, with the Q3 v Q4 widening out to 600. Huge volume went through on the Cal27 between 26150-26350 and similarly the Cal28, with a range of 228750-23000. PMX PMX pushed higher than yesterday’s close, showing a strong index gain of +726. May traded at a low of 20150 and was bid up to 20800, however it lacked support and closed at 20250. June traded in a large range between 20000 and 21500. July held a narrow $300 range, trading up to 20700, which caused the June/July spread to reach 650. Q3 printed from a low of 19800 up to 20300 back to 19800 at close. Q4 traded between 17700 and 18250. On the back end, Cal27 traded around 15000, while Cal28 saw a few clips trade at 13900. May traded 17750 - 18000, Jun 18400 - 18850, Jul 18150 - 18400 and Q3 to a high of 17900. Q4 traded between 15900 – 16200 and Q1 12250 – 12400.
